title: IntentV1 — the typed intent artifact for one goatnet
description: One document per governed goatnet at ops/consistency/intent/<goatnet>/intent.json: the RESOLVED answer to 'what is this goatnet supposed to run', with the resolution state attached to every value. Generated as the second output of ops/pins/generate-pins.py from ops/pins/fleet-pins.yaml + ops/pins/parity-capabilities.yaml + the governed group_vars; committed and --check-gated in the `fleet-pins` CI job. YAML stays the authoring surface; no consumer other than the generator parses it. Canon: docs/design/consistency-foundation.md §3 (ADR 1110 D1). SERIALIZATION IS PART OF THE CONTRACT: UTF-8, keys sorted, two-space indent, one trailing newline — CF-5 signs SHA-256 over these exact bytes (ADR 1082's pattern), so a re-serialization that changes bytes invalidates a signature. NO SECRETS: anything resolved from lookup('env', ...) renders `unreadable` with its source named and never its value.

format.description: Format discriminator. A consumer that does not recognise it refuses the document rather than guessing.

goatnet.description: The goatnet this generation describes — a key under `goatnets:` in ops/pins/fleet-pins.yaml.

members.description: The goatnet's member host-groups, in table order. These are the column keys of every `members` map below. Intent is per-goatnet with per-member columns — never per-host (design doc §3.7).

serial.description: Monotonic human-facing name of this generation. Bumped by the generator ONLY when the body changes, so regeneration with no change is a byte-no-op and the committed file stays reviewable (the name-snapshot rule, ADR 1082 §3.1). It is NOT the comparison key — `content_hash` is.

generated_at.description: UTC timestamp, moving only with `serial`. A timestamp that moved on every render would make the file drift against itself and break --check, which is exactly why the stage-1 report refuses to carry one.

ttl_seconds.description: How long a consumer may treat a fetched copy of this generation as fresh without re-fetching. Advisory: a node holding the current generation is `match` however old that generation is (design doc §5.3), so this bounds copy freshness, never correctness.

ca_id.description: The per-goatnet offline CA that CF-5 will sign this artifact with, resolved from the group_vars key named by `ca_id_var:` in fleet-pins.yaml. Null when no key is declared, when nothing resolves, or when two members resolve it to DIFFERENT values — the last of which is a real finding and is left null rather than guessed.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 over the canonical serialization of this document MINUS `serial`, `generated_at` and `content_hash`. This is the comparison key: a deterministic function of the tree that both sides can compute. Comparing on git commit instead would grade every node diverged after every doc-only merge (design doc §3.3).

sources.description: Repo-relative path -> sha256 of the exact bytes of every input file this generation was rendered from. Part of the hashed body, so an input edit is a new generation even when no resolved value moved.

history.description: The generations this one succeeds, newest first — the IDENTITY TRIPLE only, never the bodies (design doc §3.3a, applied 2026-08-04). It exists so a reader holding ONE artifact can tell `SKEW` from `unaccountable`: a generation hash present here is behind by a known count and a known age, one present nowhere is explained by nothing the reader can see. Depth is capped at 10; a node so far behind that it fell off the tail is honestly unaccountable, which is the correct answer rather than a lost one. It sits INSIDE the hashed body, so `content_hash` and the CF-5 signature cover it. OPTIONAL: an artifact published before the amendment carries none, and a reader that finds none can still grade — it just cannot separate the two grades. It is NEVER a target: no generation other than the newest is targetable, or `converged` would stop having one meaning (design doc §3.3a).

components.description: The governed deploy pins from ops/pins/fleet-pins.yaml, resolved per member.

var.description: The ansible var this component renders into group_vars/<member>/pins.yml.

artifact_type.description: ADR 1060's artifact-type dispatch, carried so a consumer can emit the RIGHT remediation pointer: image rolls back, data/cert refuse and point at restore/rotate. Declared per component in fleet-pins.yaml; defaults to `image`.

ledger_component.description: The DECLARED join key between this component and a node's ADR 1060 deploy ledger at /var/lib/goat/<name>/deploy-history.jsonl — what the CF-3 live comparison joins on. Absent means the join key is the component `name`. Explicit null means this component has NO ledger coverage (it is deployed from a playbook rather than from a role carrying the rollback-ledger meta-dependency), so it can never be observed live; it still counts in the reported denominator, which is how that coverage gap stays visible instead of silently missing. Never inferred from `var`.

render_watch.description: CF-4: the DECLARED set of rendered on-host files that are this component's config identity, from fleet-pins.yaml. Paths may embed {{ vars }} and stay LITERAL (the {{ ghcr_org }} rule) — only the deploying host resolves them, so a live reader joins render records at component granularity and uses this list's LENGTH as the coverage denominator. The expected hash is deliberately absent: a per-host render is a function of host vars and env lookups no repo-side reader may evaluate, so the node's own converge-time render manifest is the comparison baseline. The generator refuses this field on a component whose ledger_component is null — the manifest lives under /var/lib/goat/<ledger_component>/.

capabilities.description: The curated per-goatnet capability flags from ops/pins/parity-capabilities.yaml, resolved per member. Graded rows: members of one goatnet are compared.

node_shape.description: Per-node-by-design rows (ADR 1084). Carried so a consumer can explain which asymmetries are structural; NEVER graded.

retired.description: Keys asserted ABSENT across every member. Retiring a key without carrying the assertion is how it comes back.

present_in.description: Scopes where the retired key was found — empty is the compliant state. A non-empty list is a finding, not a comment.

ungoverned.description: Pin-shaped keys present in a member's group_vars but NOT rows in the fleet table. Named rather than omitted: an image the artifact stays silent about is exactly the drift it exists to prevent (design doc §3.1).

source.description: Repo-relative path of the file that defines it.

allowlisted.description: Whether the row is declared in the shrink-only tail ops/pins/unmigrated-pins.txt. False means undeclared.

declared.description: A deviation declared in the authoring surface. Its presence is what lets a consumer grade `declared` instead of `SKEW`; a deviation without a `reason:` is a schema error at the authoring surface, so one can never arrive here.

scope.description: The goatnet or member the deviation was keyed under.

value.description: The pin as committed. `{{ ghcr_org }}` stays LITERAL: the same committed string must resolve to a different org depending on which checkout deploys, so it is carried un-evaluated rather than guessed (design doc §3.1).

oneOf.description: The member deliberately does not run this component. Absence with a reason, never a missing key.

varCell.description: A group_vars value resolved for one member, with its resolution STATE attached. The three states are kept apart deliberately and a consumer holding only this artifact cannot recompute them: `unset` means there was nothing to read, `unreadable` means it was read and could not be evaluated. Collapsing them would let a missing key hide behind a templating excuse — and neither may ever reach `match`.

value.description: Normalised: booleans and boolean-ish strings render as `true`/`false`.

source.description: Where the winning value came from — a group_vars path, `group_vars/all.yml`, or `role default: <role>`.

detail.description: Why it could not be evaluated — templated, resolved from the environment, or defaulted by several roles with no single default to attribute.

why.description: Why this key earns a row, carried from the authoring surface so a consumer never has to invent the justification.

declared.description: Declared deviations for this row, keyed by the goatnet or member scope they were written against.
